title: Structural, lossless cleaning with a log
request: Home is where a problem becomes a solution: the user writes one sentence (or asks for any kind of model), brings data or not, and while the data is structured, cleaned and described in the background, a chat at the bottom asks a few questions about the real problem and an agent draws a solution workflow for this specific problem that follows the conversation. This package cleans the table in the background, without leaking anything about the outcome.
spec: draft/clean.py: names, missing-value markers, trimming, numbers and dates written as text, yes/no columns, empty rows and columns, exact duplicates, category codes; every step logged with counts. Done when the cleaning tests pass and the input frame is never changed.
plan: Write clean(frame) returning a new frame and a log, with only structural, lossless steps.
Log each step that changed something with a title, a detail and counts.
Detect numeric columns that are really category codes.
Test each step, the order of steps, and that the input frame is not changed.

decisions.decision: No imputation, scaling, encoding or outlier removal before a project exists.
decisions.why: Those learn from the data and belong inside training folds; doing them on Home would leak information from the rows that later form the holdout (rules 1 and 2).

decisions.decision: Values with leading zeros ('007', postcodes) stay text; thousands separators must come in groups of three, so '1,5' stays text while '1,234' becomes 1234.
decisions.why: Reading a code or a decimal comma as a number would change what the column means.

decisions.decision: A date must contain a digit and not be all digits.
decisions.why: Weekday names and phone numbers must not become dates.

change: dclab_rnd/draft/clean.py: clean(frame) and category_code_columns(frame); steps for names, missing markers, trimming, numbers, dates, yes/no values, empty rows and columns and exact duplicates, each logged with counts.

findings.defect: Cleaning turned yes/no columns into booleans, and two later steps crashed on them.
findings.scenario: An uploaded Telco CSV went through cleaning (Yes/No became True/False); the engine's data stage then failed on its drift check because numpy cannot take quantiles of booleans, and the column auditor crashed on a regression table with two yes/no columns because numpy refuses to subtract booleans (a 500 in the wizard).
findings.cause: Booleans count as numeric in pandas but not in numpy arithmetic, and a cleaning step made them common.
findings.fix: The engine turns boolean features into 0/1 with missing kept missing (the target stays compared as text), and the auditor compares column pairs as floats.

measurements.name: cleaning speed
measurements.gate: Cleaning a large table must take seconds.
measurements.result: A 300,000-row CSV cleaned in 2.0 s; a 200,000-line access log in 2.4 s.

outcome: Done: cleaning is structural and lossless, logged step by step, and never changes its input. The booleans it produces are now handled by the engine and the auditor.
lessons: A cleaning step that changes a type changes every consumer; run the whole flow on a real file after adding one.
